› Write a 300 word story about a lighthouse keeper. Do not use tools.


• Every evening, Mara climbed the iron stairs of Halewick Light with a kettle in one hand and a brass key in the other.
  The sea below worried the rocks like an old dog with a bone. She trimmed the wick, polished the lens, and waited for
  the first star to appear in the western pane.

  For thirty years she had kept ships from the shoals, though few captains knew her name. They knew only the white
  flash, three beats apart, promising harbor. Mara liked it that way. A keeper was not meant to be seen; she was meant
  to be believed.

  One November night, fog swallowed the island before supper. The bell buoy clanged somewhere blind and far. Then,
  beneath the wind, Mara heard a whistle: one long cry, then two short. Distress.

  The lamp sputtered. A crack in the oil pipe had opened, dripping fuel onto stone. Mara knelt, wrapped the pipe with
  her wool scarf, and burned her fingers tightening the clamp. The flame rose again, but the fog threw its light back at
  her.

  So she took the emergency lantern and went outside. Step by step, she carried the small red glow down the cliff path,
  past turf slick with spray. At the lower ledge she swung it over the abyss in the pattern sailors knew.

  An hour later, the trawler Mercy limped into the cove, hull scraped but whole. At dawn, its captain brought Mara a
  crate of oranges and stared at her bandaged hands.

  “You saved us,” he said.

  Mara looked up at the tower, where the great lens still turned, patient as the moon. “No,” she said, smiling. “I only
  kept the promise.”

  That night, when the beam swept over black water, Mara felt, for once, that the unseen could also be known and loved.
